newsitem.title: USA: UAW, GM reach tentative agreement to end strike.
newsitem.headline: UAW, GM reach tentative agreement to end strike.

text.p: The United Auto Workers union said they reached a tentative agreement with General Motors Corp. Friday night to end a parts plant strike that had forced GM to idle six assembly plants in the United States and Canada.

UAW Local 909 Financial Secretary Jim Marcum said details of the agreement would not be released until a ratification vote set for Sunday morning. The strike by 2,800 workers at the Warren, Mich., powertrain plant began at midnight Tuesday when a new agreement could be not be reached by the strike deadline.

Earlier Friday, Local 909 officials said significant progress toward an agreement had been made. The UAW has demanded that GM add several hundred workers to the plant to offset retirements and ease overtime strains. The union also wanted GM to put a cap on products it planned to outsource to outside suppliers.
The plant supplies automatic transmissions for many of GM's front-wheel-drive cars, as well as wheels and suspension control arms for both cars and light trucks.

A shortage of parts has forced GM to idle four car plants in Michigan and two at its Oshawa, Ontario, complex. The shutdowns affected about 16,500 workers, not including the strikers, and led to fears that production disruptions would spread to the rest of GM's North American assembly facilities by the end of next week.

Workers at a Delphi Interior & Lighting Systems plant in Anderson, Ind., are scheduled to ratify a new agreement Saturday. Not including the Warren and Anderson workers, GM has nine UAW locals that still do not have new three-year agreements.
